minutes.headline: Selectmen adopted a green energy policy for town buildings; the pipeline resolution was put off to February 3.
minutes.summary: Residents criticised the Green Communities task force over solar bylaw involvement, then two residents urged action against the Kinder Morgan pipeline. The board held a joint session with the task force, adopted the energy policy with a wording change, and discussed the group's charter and stalled grant projects. The town manager reported on FY15 goals and warned that the first FY16 budget will come in under target.

what_happened.line: The Select Board adopted a town green energy policy, with a revision that the board, school and library each appoint someone to audit, monitor and update procedures.
The Kinder Morgan pipeline resolution was not voted; it was put on the February 3 agenda for review.
The board declined to seat the school facilities director as a voting member of the Green Communities task force, citing policy against town employees on committees.
The board said it will formally recharge the task force as a Green Communities committee, and asked it to email the grant projects and eligibility so they can go to departments.
The town manager warned that state local aid could be hit in FY16 and that the first FY16 budget will come in under target.

why_it_matters: The energy policy sets who oversees energy use in town and school buildings, and the stalled Green Communities grant projects affect whether later installments of grant money arrive.

The town manager's warning points to a tighter FY16 budget, with free cash possibly used for current-year gaps instead of capital, which bears on services and the tax bill residents will vote on at Town Meeting.
